mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz A-Class A45 AMG engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for an A45 AMG typically costs between £2,000 and £15,000 depending on the engine code and condition. Used M133 units start from £2,000-£4,500, reconditioned from £4,500-£8,000, and fully rebuilt M139 engines from £8,000-£15,000. Labour for supply & fit adds £600-£1,200 for AMG-specialist work.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mercedes-Benz A-Class A45 AMG have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: All A45 AMG engines use timing chains, not belts. The M133 (W176) and M139 (W177) both have timing chains designed to last the life of the engine with proper maintenance. However, the M133 is known for timing chain stretch on higher-mileage units - a rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine problems in a Mercedes-Benz A-Class A45 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs of engine problems in the A45 AMG include: a rattling noise on cold start (timing chain stretch on M133), misfires or rough running (valve spring failure on M139 or ignition coil failure on M133), power loss or whistling from the engine bay (turbocharger issues), and overheating after spirited driving (cooling system strain on M139). If you experience any of these, have the car inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz A-Class A45 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A W176 A45 AMG is typically worth £10,000-£25,000 - a rebuilt M133 engine (£6,000-£12,000) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. A W177 A45 AMG is worth £20,000-£45,000 - a rebuilt M139 engine (£8,000-£15,000) is usually well within the car's value. For lower-value examples or those with multiple issues, a specialist repair may be more economical than a full replacement.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M133 and M139 engines in the A45 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M133 is the original 2.0-litre AMG engine used in the W176 A45 AMG (2013-2018), producing 360-381 hp with a twin-scroll turbocharger. The M139 is the successor introduced in the W177 A45 AMG (2019-present), producing 382-416 hp. The M139 features a rotated engine layout (turbo and exhaust at the rear), higher boost pressure (up to 2.1 bar), combined direct and port injection, and a higher rev limit of 7,200 rpm. Both are hand-built under AMG's 'One Man, One Engine' philosophy.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz A-Class A45 AMG to misfire?

acceptedAnswer.text: On M133-equipped A45 AMG models (W176, 2013-2018), misfires are most commonly caused by ignition coil failure or carbon buildup on intake valves. On M139-equipped models (W177, 2019-present), misfires are often caused by broken valve springs within the cylinder head. Faulty spark plugs or clogged fuel injectors can also cause misfires on both engines.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz A-Class A45 AMG - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The A45 AMG arrived with the third-generation W176 A-Class in 2013 as the first-ever A-Class to wear the AMG badge, powered by the hand-built M133 2.0-litre turbocharged engine - at the time, the world's most powerful production four-cylinder engine. It was replaced in 2019 by the W177-generation A45 AMG, which introduced the M139 engine - a clean-sheet design that rotated the engine 180 degrees for improved airflow and boosted power to an extraordinary 416 hp in the A45 S.

milestones.description: M133 DE20 AL, 2.0L turbo petrol, 360 hp (265 kW) - W176 A45 AMG launch; 450 Nm torque; "One Man, One Engine" hand-built; 0-62 mph in 4.6 seconds
M133 upgraded, 381 hp (280 kW) - W176 facelift; 475 Nm torque; 0-62 mph improved to 4.2 seconds
M139, 2.0L turbo petrol, 382 hp (387 PS) - W177 A45 AMG launch; 480 Nm; engine rotated 180°; 0-62 mph in 4.0 seconds
M139 S-model, 416 hp (421 PS) - A45 S AMG launch; 500 Nm; 2.1 bar boost pressure; 0-62 mph in 3.9 seconds
Facelift with M139 continuing; 8-speed DCT introduced

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes-Benz A-Class A45 AMG is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz A-Class A45 AMG Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The A45 AMG has been powered by two generations of Mercedes-AMG's 2.0-litre turbocharged engines - the M133 (W176) and the M139 (W177). Both are hand-built, high-performance units that deliver exceptional power but have well-documented weak points. Rebuilt A45 AMG engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M133 Timing Chain Stretch - Why the W176 A45 AMG Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The M133's timing chain drive can suffer from premature stretching, particularly with infrequent oil changes or aggressive operation. The chain tensioner can also lose pressure, allowing the chain to slacken. Symptoms include a rattling noise on cold start and erratic idle. If left unchecked, the chain can skip, causing piston-to-valve contact and catastrophic engine failure.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W176 A45 AMG is worth £10,000-£25,000 depending on condition and mileage. For vehicles under £12,000, a preventative chain replacement (£1,800-£3,000) is the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For higher-value examples, a rebuilt M133 with warranty (£6,000-£12,000) offers peace of mind. Given the A45 AMG's strong retained values, replacement is usually justified for well-maintained cars.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the engine on cold starts, have the timing chain inspected immediately. A preventative chain replacement at a specialist saves thousands compared to waiting for failure. Regular oil changes using the correct AMG-approved oil spec are essential to prolong chain life.

problems.h4: M133 Turbocharger & Ignition Coil Failures - Boost Loss and Misfires
problems.rootCause: The M133's BorgWarner B03G twin-scroll turbocharger can suffer from stress and wear, leading to power loss, whistling noises, and oil in the intake. Ignition coils also have a relatively low service life and can cause misfires. Carbon buildup on intake valves from the direct injection system is another common cause of misfires and flat spots.

problems.recommendation: If your A45 AMG feels sluggish, misfires, or produces a whistling noise, have the turbocharger and ignition system inspected. A £250-£500 ignition coil replacement is a cheap fix for misfires, while a £1,800-£3,000 turbocharger replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Carbon cleaning every 40,000-60,000 miles can prevent performance loss.

problems.h4: M139 Broken Valve Springs & Cooling System Issues - W177 A45 AMG Misfires and Overheating
problems.rootCause: The M139 engine has been reported to suffer from broken valve springs within the cylinder head, causing misfires, rough engine operation, difficulty starting, and Check Engine Light illumination. Cooling system strain can also lead to overheating after spirited driving, particularly if the water pump or thermostat fails. Elevated oil consumption is another reported issue.

Monitor coolant levels and temperature gauges closely, and use only OEM-spec spark plugs replaced early if performance drops.
